newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Seven judge bench of Supreme Court unanimously rejects leave to proceed in four fundamental rights applications challenging appointment of Professor Shiranee Bandaranayake. Professor Bandaranayake, the first woman to sit on the Supreme Court, was appointed last month by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
President Kumaratunga tells public servants to either co-operate in government efforts to develop country, or "quit right now".
Seven Trade unionists in police custody on charges of damaging public property and obstruction, after last week's disturbances at Steel Corporation in a Colombo suburb.
Seven judge bench of Supreme Court unanimously rejects fundamental rights appliction protesting appointment of Professor Shiranee Bandaranayake.
Central Environmental Authority rejects Ceylon Electricity Board application, to construct 150 MW hydropower plant.
Sri Lanka forces capture big LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) camp in east, in operation "Singing Fish" launched last week, defence sources say.
A number of trade unions to demonstrate on Friday against privatisation and alleged police harassment of union leaders.
Either work with dedication for which you will be justly rewarded, or go home, President Kumaratunga tells public servants.
Supreme Court rejects leave to proceed on fundamental rights applications, protesting appointment of Professor Shiranee Bandaranayake to the Supreme Court.
Employees of Steel Corporation to get all dues for 1996, following discussions between unions and new owners, Korea Heavy who bought 90 percent of the facility in October.
